track.title: Linux Fundamentals
track.description: Master the Linux command line, file system, and basic administration.

modules.title: Command Line Basics
modules.description: Navigate the terminal, manage files, and understand the shell.

lessons.title: Introduction to Linux
lessons.description: What Linux is, why it matters, and how it differs from other OSes.

lessons.title: Navigating the File System
lessons.description: Learn pwd, ls, cd, and the Linux directory hierarchy.

labs.title: CLI Basics Lab
labs.description: Practice essential terminal commands: pwd, ls, cd, mkdir, and rm.
hints: Use 'man <command>' to read the manual for any command.
Tab completion saves time — press Tab after typing partial names.
checklist: Understood the difference between relative and absolute paths

steps.title: Print Working Directory
steps.prompt: What command prints your current directory?
steps.hint: Three letters, stands for 'print working directory'.
steps.successMessage: Correct! pwd shows where you are in the filesystem.

steps.title: List Directory Contents
steps.prompt: What command lists files in the current directory?
steps.hint: Two letters. Try the basic form or the long listing.

steps.title: Create a Directory
steps.prompt: Write the command to create a directory called 'projects'.
steps.hint: The command name is short for 'make directory'.

steps.title: Change Directory
steps.prompt: Write the command to move into the 'projects' directory you just created.

quizzes.title: CLI Basics Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Test your knowledge of basic Linux commands.

questions.prompt: Which command prints the current working directory?
questions.explanation: pwd (print working directory) displays the full path of the current directory.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are valid ls flags? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: -l (long listing), -a (show hidden), and -h (human-readable sizes) are all valid. -z is not a standard ls flag.

questions.prompt: What command removes an empty directory?
questions.explanation: rmdir removes empty directories. rm -d also works on some systems.

modules.title: Users & Permissions
modules.description: Manage user accounts, groups, file ownership, and permission bits.

lessons.title: Users and Groups
lessons.description: Understand the Linux user model: UIDs, GIDs, /etc/passwd, and /etc/group.

labs.title: File Permissions Lab
labs.description: Practice reading and setting Linux file permissions with chmod and chown.
hints: Permission bits: r=4, w=2, x=1. Add them to set combined permissions.
Use 'ls -l' to see current permissions on files.

steps.title: Read File Permissions
steps.prompt: What command shows the permissions of a file named 'report.txt' in long format?
steps.hint: Use ls with a flag that shows the long listing.

steps.title: Set Permissions (Numeric)
steps.prompt: Set report.txt to owner read/write, group read-only, others no access. Use numeric mode.
steps.hint: Owner rw = 6, group r = 4, others none = 0.

steps.title: Add Execute Permission
steps.prompt: Add execute permission for the owner on a file called 'deploy.sh' using symbolic mode.

quizzes.title: Permissions Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Test your understanding of Linux file permissions.

questions.prompt: What does the permission string 'rwxr-x---' mean in numeric notation?
What command changes file ownership to user 'admin' and group 'staff' for file 'data.csv'?
questions.explanation: chown user:group file changes both owner and group.
